items.stem: If a group of students argues that the Constitution should be changed every ten or fifteen years, what would the passage suggest about their view?
A student claims that the Constitution should be completely unchangeable because it is sacred. Based on the passage, what is the most accurate response?
According to the passage, what is the key factor that makes the Indian Constitution a 'living document'?
Which of the following statements best describes the nature of the Indian Constitution according to the passage?
Based on the passage, which of the following best explains why the Indian Constitution has survived for over 69 years?
Which of the following best describes a 'flexible' constitution?
Which of the following is mentioned as a reason why the Indian Constitution has remained in use for over 69 years?
If a state legislature wants to propose an amendment to the Constitution, which of the following is true?
Which of the following is true about the amendment procedure of the Indian Constitution?
If the Lok Sabha has 545 members and an amendment bill is being voted on with 300 members present, how many members must support the bill to pass it?
According to the passage, which of the following is a principle of amending the constitution in most modern constitutions?
Which of the following best explains the purpose of requiring a special majority in both Houses of Parliament for amending the Constitution?
If an amendment to the Constitution of India aims to modify an article related to the distribution of powers between the States and the central government, what must be done according to the passage?
Based on the graphs described in the passage, which of the following statements is true about the number of amendments to the Indian Constitution?
According to the passage, which of the following is an example of a flexible part of the Constitution?
According to the passage, what is the purpose of requiring a special majority for amending the Constitution?
If a new amendment to the Constitution of India requires the consent of half the States, what does this suggest about the nature of the Indian federal system?
If the passage is correct in stating that amendments are not only due to political considerations, which of the following is most likely to be a reason for an amendment not related to politics?
Based on the passage, why might a constitutional amendment be described as 'only a technical amendment'?
According to the passage, what was the primary reason for the frequent amendments to the Constitution between 1970 and 1975?
Which of the following is not a reasonable explanation for the conflict between the legislature and the judiciary over different amendments?
According to the passage, which of the following is true about the power to amend the Constitution?
From the information that many amendments were made during 2000-2003, which conclusion can be drawn?
If the judiciary has the power to decide the validity of amendments, which of the following is the most likely outcome?
What does the passage mean when it says the Constitution is 'open to interpretations'?
If a new law is passed that goes against the basic structure of the Constitution, what would be the most likely outcome according to the passage?
According to the passage, which of the following best explains why the Constitution has remained respected and authoritative over time?
A political leader wants to make a constitutional amendment that would allow the government to control all media without any restrictions. What would the Judiciary likely do according to the passage?
Which of the following is an example of a constitutional amendment that changed the Preamble?
If a new amendment is proposed that changes the basic structure of the Constitution, what would be the outcome according to the passage?
Based on the passage, what is the role of the Judiciary in the evolution of the Constitution?
Which of the following statements about the 42nd Amendment is supported by the passage?

The passage mentions that the Constitution has remained a source of respect and authority because of the shared vision of the people and leaders. What does this imply about the role of the people in the functioning of the Constitution?
Why is the basic structure doctrine considered a form of judicial activism according to the passage?
Which of the following is an example of a technical amendment mentioned in the passage?
Which of the following is NOT a reason for making constitutional amendments according to the passage?
According to the passage, which of the following is NOT a condition for amending the Constitution of India?
What is the main idea behind referring to the Indian Constitution as a 'living document'?
Which amendment extended the duration of the Lok Sabha from five to six years?
What is the main reason the Indian Constitution is considered a living document?
Which of the following statements best explains why a constitution needs to be amended from time to time?
Which of the following statements about the theory of basic structure is correct?
Which of the following is an example of a technical amendment to the Indian Constitution?
Which of the following best explains why the Indian Constitution has been amended so many times despite the difficult procedure?
